violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. CDI: ITEMS PLACED IN COOLER. PIC RE-EDUCATED.

out_items.name: Proper date marking and disposition

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: OBSERVED NO DATE MARKING ONSITE AT THIS FACILITY. ITEMS REQUIRING DATE MARKING ARE AS FOLLOWS: BROTHS, COOKED MEATS, RAW MEAT, EGG ROLLS, RICE NOODLES, BEAN SPROUTS, COOKED TOFU, ETC.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. ALL OF THE ABOVE FOOD AND ALL OTHER TCS FOODS KEPT ONSITE FOR OVER 24HRS MUST BE DATE MARKED AS LISTED ABOVE. THIS MUST BE CORRECTED BY YOUR NEXT FOLLOW-UP INSPECTION. out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: OBSERVED COOKED RICE NOODLES PILED INTO A STRAINER “DRYING” AT ROOM TEMPERATURE AFTER COOKING AT 82F (30MIN).
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. YOU MAY ONLY COOL FOOD AS INDICATED ABOVE TO PREVENT BACTERIAL GROWTH. READ COOLING METHODS ATTACHMENT ON EMAIL. THIS ITEM MUST BE CORRECTED BY YOUR NEXT FOLLOW-UP INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Approved thawing methods used

violations.title: Proper thawing methods used for TCS Foods
violations.observation: Observed the following food thawing using an improper method: OBSERVED RAW MEAT THAWING ON THE SIDE OF THE THREE-VAT SINK.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be thawed using one of the following methods: 1) under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41F or less, 2) completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70F or below with a sufficient velocity to agitate and float off loose particles of food as long as held for period of time at a temperature of 41F or less, or 3) as part of a cooking process if the food is cooked as specified by Law or thawed in a microwave oven and immediately transferred to a conventional cooking process.

out_items.name: Food properly labeled, original container

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: OBSERVED SQUEEZE BOTTLES OF FOOD TO BE UNLABELED.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. ALL SQUEEZE BOTTLES OF FOOD MUST BE LABELED BY NEXT FOLLOW-UP INSPECTION. EAST WIND RESTAURANT (Inspection Date: 05/12/2026) Page 5 of 7

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage Prohibited under Sewer Lines
violations.observation: Food storage under sewer lines. OBSERVED BOTTLES OF WATER, POP, AND PACKAGED FOODS STORED UNDER UNSHIELDED SEWER LINE IN THE BASEMENT.
violations.corrective_action: Food may not be stored under sewer lines that are not shielded to intercept potential drips. ALL FOOD MUST BE MOVED FROM UNDERNEATH THE UNSHIELDED SEWER LINE OR THE SEWER LINE MUST BE SHIELDED AS DIRECTED DURING THE INSPECTION TO ENSURE NO CONTAMINATION OCCURS. THIS MUST BE CORRECTED BY THE FOLLOW-UP AFTER RE-OPENING.

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. OBSERVED MULTIPLE FIVE GALLON BUCKETS OF SAUCES/BROTH ON THE FLOOR IN FRONT OF THE COOKLINE AND FOOD STORED ON THE FLOOR BEHIND THE BAR.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. ALL FOOD INCLUDING POP AND WATER MUST BE STORED 6 INCHES ABOVE THE FLOOR. THIS MUST BE CORRECTED BY YOUR NEXT FOLLOW-UP AFTER RE-OPENING.

out_items.name: In-use utensils properly stored

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: OBSERVED TWO RICE SCOOPS IN TWO DIFFERENT AREAS HELD IN TEPID WATER. OBSERVED OTHER SCOOP AT BAR HELD IN TEPID WATER. OBSERVED TO-GO CONTAINERS LAYING IN DRY FOOD.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. ALL UTENSILS MUST BE STORED AS INDICATED ABOVE. THIS MUST BE CORRECTED BY YOUR NEXT FOLLOW-UP INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Single-use/single-service articles properly stored and used

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items, Stored off Floor, Clean Location
violations.observation: OBSERVED SINGLE USE ITEMS STORED ON THE FLOOR IN THE KITCHEN AND IN THE BASEMENT.

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items, Prohibited Storage Areas

ALL SINGLE USE ITMES/TO GO CONTAINERS MUST BE UNDER ONLY A SHIELDED SEWER LINE OR RELOCATED.

out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: Upon discussion with the person-in-charge, one or more of the elements of an effective employee health policy is either missing or incomplete. A complete employee health policy is required to be in place at the food establishment. At the time of this inspection, the Health Department reviewed handouts and resource information found on the Fairfax County website.
violations.corrective_action: A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. Handouts are available in the following languages: English, Arabic, Chinese (traditional), Farsi, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. If you have any questions about your employee health policy, please contact your area inspector or contact the Health Department at 703-246-2201, TTY 703-591-6435. EHS INSTRUCTED THE PIC TO DOWNLOAD AND HAVE ALL STAFF SIGN AND ACKNOWLEDGE THE POLICY BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. EHS SHOWED THE PIC THE POLICY ON THE FAIRFAX COUNTY WEBSITE. STAFF WILL DOWNLOAD A COPY TO HAVE FOR THE FOLLOW UP.

violations.corrective_action: All employees' personal care items shall be stored in a way that prevents the contamination of food and food contact surfaces through improper labeling or storage. EHS DISCUSSED TO STAFF THAT PERSONAL CARE ITEMS LIKE VITAMINS, ADVIL, LOTION, ETC NEED TO BE SEPARATELY STORED IN A LOCATION AWAY FROM FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, SINGLE SERVICE ITEMS, AND CLEAN LINENS. MANAGEMENT WILL DESIGNATE AN AREA IN THE BASEMENT STORAGE ROOM FOR EMPLOYEE’S PERSONAL ITEMS BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP;.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: EHS observed hot foods being covered and placed into reach-in refrigerators for cooling.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. PIC disposed of rice noodles being left on the counter overnight. Reviewed cooling parameters and methods with the PIC. Ensure training to staff before the follow up.

out_items.name: Food properly labeled, original container

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: 1) WORKING CONTAINERS SUCH AS SQUEEZE BOTTLES AT THE COOK LINE.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO LABEL ALL WORKING CONTAINERS, BOTTLES, SQUEEZE BOTTLES, ETC. ENSURE CORRECTION BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

out_items.name: Insects, rodents, and animals not present

violations.title: Controlling Pests, Pest Control Methods
violations.observation: EHS observed mouse dropping throughout the facility in the kitchen area, dry storage area, behind the bar, and in the basement storage area. EHS observed mouse droppings on the prep top surface of next to the wok line and inside a the 2 door reach in cooler ( turned off)
violations.corrective_action: Insects and other pests are capable of transmitting disease to people by contaminating food and food-contact surfaces. If pests are found on the premises methods shall be used to control their presence. PIC agreed to call pest control, EHS will follow up.

violations.title: Openings Protected from Pest Entry
violations.observation: EHS observed the front door the establishment is kept open for ventilation without an effective barrier to prevent pests. EHS also observed a gap along the top of the rear hallway door (near restrooms).
violations.corrective_action: Provide screens (16 mesh to 1 inch), air curtains, or other effective means to protect against the entry of insects and rodents. PIC closed front door during inspection. EHS INSTRUCTED THE PIC TO SEAL THE TOP OF THE REAR HALLWAY DOOR BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP AS THERE ARE PEST ISSUES.

violations.title: Dead or Trapped Pest Removed
violations.observation: EHS observed a pest control sticky trap with 15+ dead cockroaches attached to it.
violations.corrective_action: Remove dead rodents, birds, and insects from the premises to ensure that the establishment is clean and sanitary and to prevent carcasses from attracting other pests. PIC agreed to call pest control for service EHS will follow up after servicing.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage Prohibited in Garbage Rooms
violations.observation: EHS observed cooking oil being stored in the garbage room of the facility.
violations.corrective_action: Food may not be stored in garbage rooms. PIC agreed to remove cooking oil to an approved storage space. EAST WIND RESTAURANT (Inspection Date: 05/01/2025) Page 5 of 6

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Observed food directly stored on the floor in the walk-in refrigerator and walk-in freezer.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. EHS INSTRUCTED THE OWNER TO GET ALL FOOD 6 INCHES OFF THE FLOOR BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

out_items.name: Wiping cloths properly used and stored

violations.title: Wiping Cloths Stored in Sanitizer Solution
violations.observation: EHS observed wet wiping cloths stored on the prep top table next to the wok line
violations.corrective_action: Wet wiping cloths are to be used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces and are to be held in a chemical sanitizer solution at the appropriate concentration between uses. PIC agreed to remove the wet wiping cloths to buckets sanitizer solution.

out_items.name: In-use utensils properly stored

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: EHS observed rice scoops, and knives being stored in containers of standing non heated water (81F).
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. PIC removed rice scoops and knives and had them washed rinsed and sanitized. EHS reviewed with PIC about proper in use utensil storage. EAST WIND RESTAURANT (Inspection Date: 05/01/2025) Page 4 of 6

out_items.name: Utensils, equipment and linens properly stored, dried and handled

violations.title: Equip/Utensils/Linens, Prohibited Storage Areas
violations.observation: EHS observed pots being g stored inside the garbage room.
violations.corrective_action: Cleaned and sanitized equipment, utensils, laundered linens, and single-service items may not be stored in: 1) locker rooms, 2) toilet rooms, 3) garbage rooms, 4) mechanical rooms, 5) under sewer lines that are not shielded to intercept potential drips, 6) under leaking water lines including leaking automatic fire sprinkler heads or under lines on which water has condensed, 7) under open stairwells, or 8) under other sources of contamination. PIC agreed to move pots to approved storage space before the follow up.

violations.title: Equip/Utensils/Linens Stored off Floor, Clean Location
violations.observation: Observed equipment directly stored on the floor in the kitchen areas.
violations.corrective_action: Store clean equipment, utensils, and linens in a clean, dry location where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. EHS INSTRUCTED THE OWNER THAT NOTHING SHALL BE DIRECTLY STORED ON THE FLOOR. EVERYTHING IS PROPERLY STORED ON NSF APPROVED SHELVING UNITS OR DUNNAGE RACK. ENSURE CORRECTION BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

out_items.name: Single-use/single-service articles properly stored and used

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items No Reuse
violations.observation: EHS OBSERVED MILK CONTAINERS BEING REUSED FOR THE STORAGE OF TEA, MILANO COOKIE CONTAINERS BEING REUSED FOR THE STORAGE OF FRIED GARLIC AND SRIRACHA BOTTLES BEING REUSED FOR THE STORAGE OF VARIOUS SAUCES. EHS OBSERVED REUSE OF FRESH PEELED GARLIC CONTAINERS ALSO.
violations.corrective_action: Manufacturer containers may not be reused for secondary storage of other foods because the containers are not durable enough for multiple reuse and become uncleanable. PIC WILL DISPOSE OF THE SINGLE USE MANUFACTURERS CONTAINERS . PIC AGREED TO ONLY USE REUSABLE CONTAINERS.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Durable/Smooth Materials
violations.observation: EHS observed cardboard being used in the 1 door prep cooler across from the cook line. Cardboard observed on the floor at the cook line and on the floor of the walk in cooler and freezer.
violations.corrective_action: Non-food contact surfaces of equipment that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other foods that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a corrosion- resistant, nonabsorbent, and smooth material. EHS SPOKE WITH PIC ABOUT USING CARDBOARD IN THE FACILITY AND CHANGING IT EVERY 24 HOURS, PIC AGREED TO REMOVE THE CARDBOARD FROM THE FLOOR OF THE COOK-LINE, INSIDE THE 1 DOOR PREP TOP COOLER AND FROM THE. FLOOR OF THE WALK IN COOLER AND FREEZER.

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following refrigeration unit is not operating properly and is unable to maintain cold food at or below 41F: Walk in cooler (46F) and 1 door prep top cooler (61F).
violations.corrective_action: Repair/adjust the unit so it is able to maintain foods at or below 41F. Do not use the unit to store time/temperature control for safety foods while it is not operating properly. PIC AGREED TO HAVE 1 DOOR PREP TOP COOLER AND WALK IN COOLER REPAIRED BY NEXT INSPECTION SO THEY CAN MAINTAIN AN AIR TEMPERATURE OF 34f-38f.

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following equipment is not operating properly and/or is in poor repair: OBSERVED (5) LIGHTS INSIDE THE VENT HOOD ABOVE THE COOKLINE NOT TURNING ON.
violations.corrective_action: Equipment shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. PIC AGREED TO HAVE THE VENTILATION HOOD ABOVE THE COOKLINE CLEANED AND LIGHTBULBS REPLACED

violations.title: Cutting Board, When to Resurface or Discard
violations.observation: The cutting board(s) on the PREP TABLE NEXT TO THE 1 DOOR PREP TOP COOLER AND ON THE 3 DOOR PREP TOP COOLER are heavily scratched and scored. The food contact surface is no longer easily cleaned and sanitized due to condition.
violations.corrective_action: Surfaces such as cutting blocks and boards that are subject to scratching and scoring shall be resurfaced if they can no longer be effectively cleaned and sanitized, or discarded if they are not capable of being resurfaced. PIC AGREED TO REPLACE THE CUTTING BOARDS BY NEXT INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Non-food contact surfaces clean

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces Kept Clean
violations.observation: EHS observed the following in need of cleaning: 1) THE 2 DOOR SLIDING BAR COOLER AT THE BAR AREA USED FOR DRINK STORAGE, 2) INTERIORS OF UNUSED REFRIGERATION UNITS, 3) FLOOR OF THE WALK-IN UNITS, 4) SHELVING AND STORAGE UNITS, 5) EXTERIORS OF EQUIPMENT TO INCLUDE COOK LINE, FOOD PROCESSOR, TOASTER OVEN, MICROWAVE OVENS, RICE COOKERS, 6) INTERIORS OF MICROWAVE OVENS, TOASTER OVENS,
violations.corrective_action: Nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. PIC AGREED TO THOROUGHLY CLEAN AND SANITIZE ALL AREAS OF THE KITCHEN, EQUIPMENT, ETC BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

out_items.name: Hot and cold water available, adequate pressure

violations.title: Hot Water Capacity to Meet Peak Demands
violations.observation: The permit holder has a 4500 TOTAL WATT electric water heater. This unit is severely undersized for the peak hot water demands required.
violations.corrective_action: Within 30 days, the permit holder shall replace or upgrade the water heater with a unit that meets the following design and capacity requirements: (1) Commercial grade, (2) Minimum of 50 gallon storage tank, (3) Minimum recovery rate of 104gph of 120f at an 80f rise@, and (4) Specifications and installation meet National Sanitation Foundation (NSF) Standard 5. The permit holder shall provide the Health Department with the specifications (cut sheet) for the replacement water heater and obtain approval prior to purchase and installation. Please be reminded that equipment replacement or addition is not allowed without prior approval by the Health Department. EHS INSTRUCTED THE OWNER THAT THE WATER HEATER IS SEVERELY DEFICIENT. REPLACE WITH AT LEAST A 24 KW ELECTRIC WATER HEATER BEFORE THE NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION IN APPROXIMATELY 6 MONTHS.

out_items.name: Plumbing installed, proper backflow devices

violations.title: Backflow Prevention, Approved Device Provided
violations.observation: Observed the lack of an approved backflow prevention device on the water supply system connecting to the ice machine at the bar.
violations.corrective_action: A plumbing system shall be installed to preclude backflow of a solid, liquid, or gas contaminant into the water supply system at each point of use at the food establishment, including on a hose bib if a hose is attached or on a hose bib if a hose is not attached and backflow prevention is required by Law by installing an approved backflow prevention device as specified under 5-202.14. PIC AGREED TO CALL A PLUMBER TO INSTALL A BACK FLOW PREVENTION DEVICE. ENSURE CORRECTION BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

violations.title: Plumbing System, Maintain Good Repair
violations.observation: Observed both the bar and kitchen hand sinks without running water.
violations.corrective_action: A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair. EHS INSTRUCTED THE OWNER TO HAVE BOTH HAND SINKS FUNCTIONING AS REQUIRED FOR PROPER HAND WASHING PROCEDURES. ENSURE CORRECTION BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

Food-contact surfaces cleaned and sanitized

violations.corrective_action: All utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use and after cleaning. EMPLOYEE RAN WOK THROUGH DISHWASHER, WHICH WAS OBSERVED AT 50 PPM CHLORINE.

out_items.name: Approved thawing methods used

violations.title: Proper thawing methods used for TCS Foods
violations.observation: Observed the following food thawing using an improper method: EHS OBSERVED MEATBALLS THAWING AT ROOM TEMPERATURE IN STILL WATER.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be thawed using one of the following methods: 1) under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41F or less, 2) completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70F or below with a sufficient velocity to agitate and float off loose particles of food as long as held for period of time at a temperature of 41F or less, or 3) as part of a cooking process if the food is cooked as specified by Law or thawed in a microwave oven and immediately transferred to a conventional cooking process. PIC DRAINED WATER AND PLACED MEATBALLS IN COOLER.

violations.corrective_action: Insects and other pests are capable of transmitting disease to people by contaminating food and food-contact surfaces.
